module.name: hal_crypto
module.brief: Cryptographic operation-class APIs and driver lifecycle.
module.details: All cryptographic operations use unlocked thread context and may block. The HLD checks call parameters and manages the driver lifecycle. Stream contexts are defined and managed by the LLD, which also checks context state. Parameter and context-state violations are programming errors caught by debug checks and assertions; return codes report only conditions that depend on runtime data or on the backend. The driver does not manage keys: key zero is a volatile transient key and the only key every driver can load with cryKeyLoad(). Other identifiers refer to keys the backend provides in an unspecified way, for example provisioned into an HSM; whether some of them can also be loaded, and with which lifetime, is backend-defined. The LLD rejects identifiers without a key and keys unsuitable for an operation. Operations using a loadable key hold it, and loading that key fails while it is held; callers sharing a driver serialize loading and the begin that uses the key, for example with drvLock(). Callers must serialize access to each operation context. Different contexts may be used concurrently from different threads; the driver remains in HAL_DRV_STATE_READY while streams are open. Hardware and other resources are accounted by the LLD, which reports CRY_ERR_BUSY when a resource is exhausted and may reject live reconfiguration while resources are in use. drvStop() requires that no call is in progress; it reclaims all resources and invalidates every open stream, and invalidated contexts behave as idle. Begin functions initialize the context they receive, which must not hold an active stream. Before disposal, abort or stop using all contexts. LLD extension fields and APIs may implement additional behavior without changing the common operation interface. Caller buffers must remain valid for each synchronous call. This API is not source or binary compatible with the legacy HAL Crypto API.

define.brief: Unsupported algorithm, capability or key operation.

typedef.name: crykey_t
typedef.brief: Key identifier.
typedef.details: CRY_KEY_TRANSIENT is a volatile key, erased by drvStop(), that every driver can load with cryKeyLoad(). Other identifiers are defined by the backend, which provides their keys in an unspecified way; loading some of them may be possible, with a backend-defined lifetime. The driver never generates, exports or deletes keys. The HLD passes identifiers to the LLD unchecked.

typedef.name: cry_operation_t
typedef.brief: Caller-owned stream context, defined by the LLD.
typedef.details: The LLD provides the complete structure definition in its header, so the size is known and contexts can be allocated statically or on the stack. Fields are private to the LLD; the HLD does not inspect them. A begin function initializes the context; its previous content is ignored, so fresh storage needs no initialization. Every return from a begin function, including failures, leaves the context initialized. Beginning on a context that holds an active stream is a programming error that leaks the resources of that stream. Do not copy a live context and do not access it concurrently.

typedef.name: cry_job_t
typedef.brief: Backend single-call descriptor.
typedef.details: Only the parameter member selected by kind may be inspected. Input pointers are borrowed until the call returns. Output capacity and actual length are separate. Signature encoding is RSA modulus-sized big-endian bytes, or ECDSA fixed-width big-endian r followed by s. Agreement and derivation return bytes to the supplied output buffer.

field.name: kind
field.brief: Operation kind selecting the valid parameter member.

field.name: input
field.brief: Borrowed message, digest, ciphertext or ECDH peer public point.

field.name: signature
field.brief: Borrowed signature to verify; unused by other operation kinds.

field.name: output
field.brief: Caller-owned signature or asymmetric encryption/decryption output.

field.name: output_length
field.brief: Receives the actual output length in bytes.

unionfield.name: params
unionfield.brief: Parameters selected by the operation kind.

field.name: signature
field.brief: Parameters for signature generation or verification.

field.name: asymmetric
field.brief: Parameters for asymmetric encryption or decryption.

class.name: hal_crypto_driver
class.brief: Crypto driver with independent operation contexts.

dispose.implementation: chDbgAssert(self->state == HAL_DRV_STATE_STOP, "dispose of active crypto driver");

method.implementation: /* The LLD reclaims all resources and invalidates open streams.*/ cry_lld_stop(self);
/* The LLD rejects live reconfiguration while resources are in use.*/ return cry_lld_setcfg(self, (const hal_crypto_config_t *)config);
/* The LLD rejects live reconfiguration while resources are in use.*/ return cry_lld_selcfg(self, cfgnum);

function.name: cryInit
function.brief: Initializes the Crypto subsystem.
function.implementation: cry_lld_init();

function.name: cryGetCapabilities
function.brief: Queries per-driver algorithm capabilities.
function.param: Receives capabilities; cleared when the query fails.
function.return: HAL_RET_SUCCESS or a Crypto error code.
function.retval: The algorithm is supported, capabilities returned.
The algorithm is not supported by this driver.

function.name: cryKeyLoad
function.brief: Loads a key.
function.details: CRY_KEY_TRANSIENT can always be loaded: it is volatile and erased by drvStop(). Whether other identifiers can be loaded, and with which lifetime, is backend-defined; identifiers that cannot be loaded are rejected with CRY_ERR_UNSUPPORTED. Operations using a loadable key hold it, from begin to finalization or abort for streams and for the duration of the call for single-call operations; loading a key fails while it is held, so an operation always uses the key it started with. Loading and the begin using the key are not atomic: callers sharing a driver serialize them, for example with drvLock(). The LLD consumes the material before returning and checks its encoding and mathematical validity. Key parameters are checked at runtime because they usually describe imported material.
function.param: Key identifier, CRY_KEY_TRANSIENT or a loadable backend key.
Encoded key material size, in bytes.
Encoded key material, consumed before return.
function.return: HAL_RET_SUCCESS or a Crypto error code.
function.retval: Invalid key parameters or key material.
The identifier cannot be loaded by this backend.
The key is held by an operation.

function.name: cryHashBegin
function.brief: Starts a hash stream.
function.param: Caller-owned operation context, initialized by this call.
function.return: HAL_RET_SUCCESS or a Crypto error code.

function.name: cryCipherBegin
function.brief: Starts an unpadded symmetric cipher stream.
function.param: Caller-owned operation context, initialized by this call.
Key identifier, CRY_KEY_TRANSIENT or a backend key.
function.return: HAL_RET_SUCCESS or a Crypto error code.

function.name: cryMacBegin
function.brief: Starts a MAC generation or verification stream.
function.details: Tag size is explicit; the LLD reports unsupported tag sizes.
function.param: Caller-owned operation context, initialized by this call.
Key identifier, CRY_KEY_TRANSIENT or a backend key.
True for verification, false for generation.
Tag size, from one byte up to the algorithm output size.
function.return: HAL_RET_SUCCESS or a Crypto error code.

function.name: cryAeadBegin
function.brief: Starts authenticated encryption or decryption.
function.details: All lengths are bytes. CCM requires declared AAD and payload totals. GCM permits CRY_LENGTH_UNKNOWN. Backends enforce further limits. Decryption output must remain quarantined until cryAeadVerify() succeeds.
function.param: Caller-owned operation context, initialized by this call.
Key identifier, CRY_KEY_TRANSIENT or a backend key.
function.return: HAL_RET_SUCCESS or a Crypto error code.
function.retval: The declared CCM payload size exceeds the length field selected by the nonce size, reported by the LLD.

function.name: cryHashUpdate
function.brief: Adds bytes to a hash stream.
function.details: A backend error aborts the stream.
function.param: Input buffer, or NULL when its size is zero.
function.return: HAL_RET_SUCCESS or a Crypto error code.

function.name: cryMacUpdate
function.brief: Adds bytes to a MAC stream.
function.details: A backend error aborts the stream.
function.param: Input buffer, or NULL when its size is zero.
function.return: HAL_RET_SUCCESS or a Crypto error code.

function.name: cryCipherUpdate
function.brief: Processes a cipher payload fragment.
function.details: Input and output must not overlap unless the backend explicitly supports the overlap. A backend error aborts the stream.
function.param: Input buffer, or NULL when its size is zero.
Output buffer, or NULL when its capacity is zero.
Receives the number of bytes produced, or zero on failure.
function.return: HAL_RET_SUCCESS or a Crypto error code.

function.name: cryAeadUpdate
function.brief: Processes an AEAD payload fragment.
function.details: Input and output must not overlap unless the backend explicitly supports the overlap. A backend error aborts the stream. AEAD decryption output is provisional and must not be released to an untrusted consumer before verification.
function.param: Input buffer, or NULL when its size is zero.
Output buffer, or NULL when its capacity is zero.
Receives the number of bytes produced, or zero on failure.
function.return: HAL_RET_SUCCESS or a Crypto error code.

function.name: cryAeadUpdateAAD
function.brief: Adds associated data before the first nonempty payload fragment.
function.details: A backend error aborts the stream.
function.param: Associated data, or NULL when its size is zero.
function.return: HAL_RET_SUCCESS or a Crypto error code.

function.name: cryHashFinal
function.brief: Finalizes a hash stream and releases its resources.
function.details: The context is idle on return, on success or failure.
function.param: Output buffer capacity, at least the digest size.
Receives the digest size, or zero on failure.
function.return: HAL_RET_SUCCESS or a Crypto error code.

function.name: cryCipherFinal
function.brief: Finalizes a cipher stream and releases its resources.
function.details: The context is idle on return, on success or failure.
function.param: Output buffer, or NULL when its capacity is zero.
Receives the number of bytes produced, or zero on failure.
function.return: HAL_RET_SUCCESS or a Crypto error code.

function.name: cryMacFinal
function.brief: Finalizes a MAC generation stream and releases its resources.
function.details: The context is idle on return, on success or failure.
function.param: Output buffer capacity, at least the tag size selected at Begin.
Receives the tag size, or zero on failure.
function.return: HAL_RET_SUCCESS or a Crypto error code.

function.name: cryMacVerify
function.brief: Verifies a MAC and retires the stream.
function.details: The tag is message data: a tag whose size differs from the size selected at Begin is an authentication failure, not a programming error. The backend compares tags in constant time. The context is idle on return, on success or failure.
function.param: Received tag, or NULL when its size is zero.
function.return: HAL_RET_SUCCESS or a Crypto error code.
function.retval: The tag does not authenticate the message.

function.name: cryAeadFinal
function.brief: Finalizes AEAD encryption and generates its tag.
function.details: tag_size must equal the size selected at Begin; output receives any deferred payload bytes. The context is idle on return, on success or failure.
function.param: Output buffer, or NULL when its capacity is zero.
Receives the number of bytes produced, or zero on failure.
Tag size selected at Begin, in bytes.
function.return: HAL_RET_SUCCESS or a Crypto error code.

function.name: cryAeadVerify
function.brief: Verifies the AEAD tag and retires the stream.
function.details: Only successful verification authenticates all provisional plaintext from this operation. On failure the caller must discard and erase it. The tag is message data: a tag whose size differs from the size selected at Begin is an authentication failure. The context is idle on return, on success or failure.
function.param: Output buffer, or NULL when its capacity is zero.
Receives the number of bytes produced, or zero on failure.
Received tag, or NULL when its size is zero.
function.return: HAL_RET_SUCCESS or a Crypto error code.
function.retval: The tag does not authenticate the message.

function.name: cryOperationAbort
function.brief: Aborts any operation class; aborting an idle context is harmless.
function.details: Valid on any context initialized by a begin function: active, finalized, failed or invalidated by drvStop(), while the driver object exists. Not valid on storage never passed to a begin function. No concurrent call may be executing on this context. On return all LLD accesses have completed, intermediate secrets are erased and the context is idle.
function.param: Operation context previously initialized by a begin function.
function.implementation:
chDbgCheck(op != NULL);
cry_lld_abort(op);

function.name: crySignDigest
function.brief: Signs a precomputed digest.
function.details: The explicit algorithm includes its hash. RSA-PSS uses MGF1 with that hash and an explicit salt length. RSA signatures are modulus-sized big-endian bytes; ECDSA is fixed-width big-endian r || s. Backends validate key-dependent lengths and scheme parameters.
function.param: Key identifier, CRY_KEY_TRANSIENT or a backend key.
Signature parameters, or NULL for defaults (zero salt).
Digest size, equal to the algorithm hash size.
Output buffer, or NULL when its capacity is zero.
Receives the signature size, or zero on failure.
function.return: HAL_RET_SUCCESS or a Crypto error code.
function.retval: The key-dependent signature does not fit.

function.name: crySignMessage
function.brief: Signs a message using the selected signature scheme.
function.details: The explicit algorithm includes its hash. RSA-PSS uses MGF1 with that hash and an explicit salt length. RSA signatures are modulus-sized big-endian bytes; ECDSA is fixed-width big-endian r || s. Backends validate key-dependent lengths and scheme parameters.
function.param: Key identifier, CRY_KEY_TRANSIENT or a backend key.
Signature parameters, or NULL for defaults (zero salt).
Message, or NULL when its size is zero.
Output buffer, or NULL when its capacity is zero.
Receives the signature size, or zero on failure.
function.return: HAL_RET_SUCCESS or a Crypto error code.
function.retval: The key-dependent signature does not fit.

function.name: cryVerifyDigest
function.brief: Verifies a signature over a precomputed digest.
function.details: The explicit algorithm includes its hash. RSA-PSS uses MGF1 with that hash and an explicit salt length. RSA signatures are modulus-sized big-endian bytes; ECDSA is fixed-width big-endian r || s. The signature is message data: malformed or wrongly sized signatures fail verification.
function.param: Key identifier, CRY_KEY_TRANSIENT or a backend key.
Signature parameters, or NULL for defaults (zero salt).
Digest size, equal to the algorithm hash size.
Received signature, or NULL when its size is zero.
function.return: HAL_RET_SUCCESS or a Crypto error code.

function.name: cryVerifyMessage
function.brief: Verifies a signature over a message.
function.details: The explicit algorithm includes its hash. RSA-PSS uses MGF1 with that hash and an explicit salt length. RSA signatures are modulus-sized big-endian bytes; ECDSA is fixed-width big-endian r || s. The signature is message data: malformed or wrongly sized signatures fail verification.
function.param: Key identifier, CRY_KEY_TRANSIENT or a backend key.
Signature parameters, or NULL for defaults (zero salt).
Message, or NULL when its size is zero.
Received signature, or NULL when its size is zero.
function.return: HAL_RET_SUCCESS or a Crypto error code.

function.name: cryAsymEncrypt
function.brief: Encrypts using an asymmetric encryption scheme.
function.details: RSA-OAEP uses the selected hash for both OAEP and MGF1. The backend enforces modulus-dependent bounds.
function.param: Key identifier, CRY_KEY_TRANSIENT or a backend key.
OAEP parameters, or NULL for no label.
Plaintext, or NULL when its size is zero.
Output buffer, or NULL when its capacity is zero.
Receives the ciphertext size, or zero on failure.
function.return: HAL_RET_SUCCESS or a Crypto error code.
function.retval: The plaintext exceeds the key-dependent limit.
The key-dependent ciphertext does not fit.

function.name: cryAsymDecrypt
function.brief: Decrypts using an asymmetric encryption scheme.
function.details: RSA-OAEP uses the selected hash for both OAEP and MGF1. The ciphertext is message data: the backend rejects malformed encodings with CRY_ERR_ARGUMENT without reporting padding details.
function.param: Key identifier, CRY_KEY_TRANSIENT or a backend key.
OAEP parameters, or NULL for no label.
Ciphertext, or NULL when its size is zero.
Output buffer, or NULL when its capacity is zero.
Receives the plaintext size, or zero on failure.
function.return: HAL_RET_SUCCESS or a Crypto error code.

function.name: cryKeyAgreement
function.brief: Computes an ECDH shared secret.
function.details: Peer encoding is an uncompressed SEC1 point on the private key curve. The peer point is message data: the LLD validates it and reports invalid points with CRY_ERR_ARGUMENT. Output is the full-width big-endian x coordinate. The caller owns the secret output and its lifetime.
function.param: Key identifier, CRY_KEY_TRANSIENT or a backend key.
Encoded peer public-key size, in bytes.
Encoded peer public key, or NULL when its size is zero.
Output buffer for the shared secret.
Receives the secret length, or zero on failure.
function.return: HAL_RET_SUCCESS or a Crypto error code.
function.retval: The curve-dependent secret does not fit.

function.name: cryDeriveKey
function.brief: Derives output bytes using HKDF.
function.details: Performs extract and expand using the selected hash. The size parameter is the requested output length, not merely buffer capacity. The caller owns the derived bytes and their lifetime.
function.param: Key identifier, CRY_KEY_TRANSIENT or a backend key.
HKDF parameters, or NULL for no salt and no context information.
Number of bytes to derive, from 1 to 255 times the hash size.
Output buffer with at least size bytes.
function.return: HAL_RET_SUCCESS or a Crypto error code.

function.name: cry_key_params_valid
function.brief: Checks the mathematical description of key material.
function.return: True if the parameter combination is valid.

function.name: cry_buffer_valid
function.brief: Checks a pointer/length pair.
function.param: Buffer pointer, may be NULL only when the size is zero.
function.return: True if the pair is consistent.
function.implementation: return (size == 0U) || (buf != NULL);

function.name: cry_algorithm_class
function.brief: Identifies known algorithms without consulting key metadata.
function.return: The operation class, CRY_CLASS_NONE for unknown selectors.
function.implementation: switch (algorithm) { case CRY_ALG_AES_ECB: case CRY_ALG_AES_CBC: case CRY_ALG_AES_CFB128: case CRY_ALG_AES_CTR: return CRY_CLASS_CIPHER; case CRY_ALG_AES_GCM: case CRY_ALG_AES_CCM: return CRY_CLASS_AEAD; case CRY_ALG_AES_CMAC: case CRY_ALG_HMAC_SHA256: case CRY_ALG_HMAC_SHA384: case CRY_ALG_HMAC_SHA512: return CRY_CLASS_MAC; case CRY_ALG_SHA1: case CRY_ALG_SHA224: case CRY_ALG_SHA256: case CRY_ALG_SHA384: case CRY_ALG_SHA512: return CRY_CLASS_HASH; case CRY_ALG_RSA_PSS_SHA256: case CRY_ALG_RSA_PSS_SHA384: case CRY_ALG_RSA_PSS_SHA512: case CRY_ALG_RSA_PKCS1_SHA256: case CRY_ALG_RSA_PKCS1_SHA384: case CRY_ALG_RSA_PKCS1_SHA512: case CRY_ALG_ECDSA_SHA256: case CRY_ALG_ECDSA_SHA384: case CRY_ALG_ECDSA_SHA512: return CRY_CLASS_SIGNATURE; case CRY_ALG_RSA_OAEP_SHA256: case CRY_ALG_RSA_OAEP_SHA384: case CRY_ALG_RSA_OAEP_SHA512: return CRY_CLASS_ASYMMETRIC; case CRY_ALG_ECDH: return CRY_CLASS_AGREEMENT; case CRY_ALG_HKDF_SHA256: case CRY_ALG_HKDF_SHA384: case CRY_ALG_HKDF_SHA512: return CRY_CLASS_DERIVATION; default: return CRY_CLASS_NONE; }

function.name: cry_digest_size
function.brief: Returns the fixed digest or MAC size.
function.return: The hash output size, zero for algorithms without one.
function.implementation: switch (algorithm) { case CRY_ALG_SHA1: return 20U; case CRY_ALG_SHA224: return 28U; case CRY_ALG_AES_CMAC: return 16U; case CRY_ALG_HMAC_SHA256: case CRY_ALG_SHA256: case CRY_ALG_RSA_PSS_SHA256: case CRY_ALG_RSA_PKCS1_SHA256: case CRY_ALG_ECDSA_SHA256: case CRY_ALG_RSA_OAEP_SHA256: case CRY_ALG_HKDF_SHA256: return 32U; case CRY_ALG_HMAC_SHA384: case CRY_ALG_SHA384: case CRY_ALG_RSA_PSS_SHA384: case CRY_ALG_RSA_PKCS1_SHA384: case CRY_ALG_ECDSA_SHA384: case CRY_ALG_RSA_OAEP_SHA384: case CRY_ALG_HKDF_SHA384: return 48U; case CRY_ALG_HMAC_SHA512: case CRY_ALG_SHA512: case CRY_ALG_RSA_PSS_SHA512: case CRY_ALG_RSA_PKCS1_SHA512: case CRY_ALG_ECDSA_SHA512: case CRY_ALG_RSA_OAEP_SHA512: case CRY_ALG_HKDF_SHA512: return 64U; default: return 0U; }

function.name: cry_signature_valid
function.brief: Checks signature parameters independently of the key.
function.param: Signature parameters, or NULL for defaults.
function.return: True if the parameters are valid for the algorithm.
